After reading the full discharged solve artifact, the current graph, and the anchor's exact model definitions, I confirm the verdict.

The existing bounded-margin theorem spine is mathematically sound and essentially maximal within its declared class. The ≤11-candidate certificate covers dependent rows, unbounded sectors, lines, points, diffusion-boundary attainment, and norm equality. The equal-variance thresholds, joint-only construction, asymmetric contact, measurable finite-sample inversion, singleton recovery, contact geometry, and matching root-n Gaussian obstruction are genuinely proved. No material rate, constant, or additional elbow is missing there.

The material omission is a sharper headline over the anchor's actual class. Van Seeventer-Salehkaleybar assume the generator-sign convention BΣ + ΣBᵀ = −D, with B Hurwitz, D positive diagonal, t-faithful Σ, and structural minimality supp(B)=E; they impose neither fixed normalized beta-min nor a drift-norm cap. Their definitions explicitly require t-faithfulness and full support (Definitions 2.1 and 2.3, https://arxiv.org/pdf/2603.08311). The note instead studies a proper bounded-margin class with η>0 and M<∞, adds κ for inference, omits explicit t-faithfulness, and does not require nonzero diagonal self-loops. Trace-one itself is only a gauge and is not the mismatch.

The proposed published-class theorem is true under the exact sign and support conventions. Let B=−A, where A is the note's mean-reversion matrix; then products and support are unchanged, while B has the anchor's sign convention and is Hurwitz. For the complete bivariate two-cycle with both self-loops, t-faithfulness forces t≠0. Fix any d∈(0,1). If t>0, every −dt/(2s) < q < (1−d)t/(2u) gives A12<0 and A21<0, hence B12>0 and B21>0. If t<0, the reversed endpoint interval gives A12>0 and A21>0, hence B12<0 and B21<0. Thus positive product is always compatible. Choosing q outside the interval gives opposite off-diagonal signs and hence negative product. The two possible q values at which A11 or A22 vanishes can be avoided because each admissible interval or ray contains infinitely many other points. Therefore supp(B)=E, D is strictly positive diagonal, stability follows from the Lyapunov equation, and every published-compatible Σ admits both product polarities: Ppub(Σ)={−1,+1}.

This exactly answers the anchor's graph-level open direction for the bivariate two-cycle. The current joint-only conclusion does not transfer upward to the unrestricted published fiber: without η and M, same-sign witnesses reappear for every t≠0. Its root-n singleton frontier is consequently a bounded-margin phenomenon, not a published-class frontier. Conversely, its lower bound remains valid for the declared restricted problem, but broadening the compatible fiber changes the set-valued target to the constant {−1,+1}.
